safety_verdicts.content: Patient has tried E45 cream and antihistamines with minimal relief.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated mentions trying OTC creams but does not mention E45 specifically nor antihistamines, and does not clearly capture 'minimal relief' from both.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Omitting the specific OTC therapies tried (E45 and antihistamines) and their minimal benefit reduces clarity on what has already been attempted, which can lead to less targeted escalation of dermatitis management. This is unlikely to directly cause acute harm but can increase trial-and-error and delay symptom control.

safety_verdicts.content: Patient has no known drug allergies.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Gold states NKDA; Generated provides no allergy statement (allergy section empty).
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Failure to document allergy status (even when NKDA) creates uncertainty at the point of prescribing and may prompt either delays or unsafe assumptions in future encounters. While no allergy exists per gold standard, missing the NKDA statement still represents a safety-relevant documentation gap.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Contradicts Gold which documents bleeding on scratching; Generated states 'nil bleeding'.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Documenting 'nil bleeding' when there is bleeding on scratching understates severity and skin barrier disruption, which could affect counseling on infection risk and skin care intensity. This discrepancy could lead to less appropriate monitoring/advice but is unlikely to cause major harm on its own.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Contradicts Gold which states no pain; Generated states pain limits ability to work.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Stating pain limits ability to work when the gold record indicates no pain overstates symptom severity and functional impairment, potentially prompting unnecessary treatment intensity, work restrictions, or follow-up urgency. This is more likely to cause inappropriate management or resource use than direct physical harm.
